summary: ING sits clearly with the traditional banks on these measured features (position score 0.21), and its distinctive traits are the volume of figures it quotes (25.5 per page against a peer mean of 12.15), a mobile-first design and student/youth targeting (1.0 against a peer mean of 0.38 on both). Its clearest deficit is the number of calls to action (2.0 against 13.38), and it is the only measured page set with no comparison table at all. The comparison is confounded by product family and language, the capture covers a single day, and no performance data exists, so every item below is a hypothesis ING could test rather than a proven cause.

recommendations.title: Add calls to action throughout the current-account pages
recommendations.finding: ING's pages carry 2.0 calls to action on average against a peer mean of 13.38, a gap of about 1.06 standard deviations and the largest single deficit in the comparison; the same signal appears in ING's market-wide signature, where Calls to action sit roughly one standard deviation below the market.
recommendations.recommendation: Place a clearly labelled call to action after each major block on the page - one primary open-an-account action plus lighter secondary actions - so a visitor never has to scroll back to the top to act.

recommendations.title: Add a comparison table to the pack pages
recommendations.finding: No comparison table was detected on ING's pages (0.0), while the peer mean is 0.38; ING's pages are also long at 9,465 px against a peer mean of 6,414 px, so the differences between packs currently have to be carried by prose alone.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a compact comparison table of the current-account packs - fees, card, included services - near the top of the page, and keep the longer explanatory prose below it.

recommendations.title: Shorten the campaign pages
recommendations.finding: Page length is 9,465 px against a peer mean of 6,414 px, about 0.91 standard deviations above peers; combined with the low number of Calls to action, the extra length is not being converted into actions.
recommendations.recommendation: Collapse or cut secondary sections so the pack offer, its price and the next step all fit within the first screens, and move supporting detail into expandable blocks.

recommendations.title: Extend the mobile-first and fast-sign-up message to every page variant
recommendations.finding: ING scores 1.0 on Designed mobile-first against a peer mean of 0.38 and 0.5 on Promises fast digital sign-up against a peer mean of 0.15, both above peers; market-wide, Designed mobile-first is one of the features that separates challengers from traditional banks.
recommendations.recommendation: Apply the mobile-first layout and the fast digital sign-up statement consistently across all current-account page variants, in both French and Dutch, rather than on a subset, and restate the sign-up promise at the point of the call to action.

recommendations.title: Cut back on the number of quoted figures
recommendations.finding: ING quotes 25.5 figures and percentages per page against a peer mean of 12.15, about 1.62 standard deviations above peers, and Figures and percentages quoted is ING's largest market-wide signature at roughly 1.4 standard deviations above the market.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep only the figures that drive the decision - fee, rate, welcome offer - in the main body of the page and move the rest into one small-print disclosure block, so the page reads as an offer rather than a data sheet.

recommendations.title: Carry the student and youth angle onto the main account page
recommendations.finding: ING scores 1.0 on Targets students or young people against a peer mean of 0.38, the second-largest element of ING's market-wide signature at about 1.2 standard deviations above the market.
recommendations.recommendation: Make the youth and student framing explicit on the dedicated young-customers page and mirror the same wording into the main current-account page, so the offer is visible to visitors who do not land on the youth page.

recommendations.title: Complete the action stage of the campaign structure
recommendations.finding: Campaign structure completeness (AIDA) is 3.5 against a peer mean of 2.71 and Makes the offer feel worth having scores 1.0 against a peer mean of 0.43, so the desire stage is well covered while Calls to action is the weakest measured leg of the structure.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the current desire-building copy and add the missing action layer: a visible next step after each benefit block, with the price or fee restated at the point of action.

recommendations.title: Have the current-account page ready for the early-September window
recommendations.finding: Search interest for ING's current account was flagged in late August and early September 2026, in the same window as the Level up your banking repositioning and the new ING Go, More, Extra and Max packs. This is a timing hypothesis to verify, not evidence that any page worked.
recommendations.recommendation: Make sure the current-account page, in both languages, names the current pack line-up in its opening block before that window, so someone arriving from a search for the account lands on a page using the pack language.
recommendations.market_context: Belgium, weekly window 2021-09-12 to 2026-09-13: a Sustained trend for 'compte à vue ING' on 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-06, an Isolated spike for 'ING zichtrekening' on 2026-09-06 (value 7, score 1.63), and further sustained current-account signals on 2026-09-13.

recommendations.title: Sequence the savings page update with the current-account page
recommendations.finding: Savings search terms were also flagged in the same window, with a shorter delay from the campaign than the current-account terms. Hypothesis to verify: the savings page may be receiving part of the same wave of interest and should not be updated after the current-account page.
recommendations.recommendation: Give the savings page the same pack-level treatment as the current-account page - refreshed opening message and a visible next step - and release the two updates together rather than in sequence.
recommendations.market_context: Belgium, same weekly window 2021-09-12 to 2026-09-13: a Sustained trend for 'compte épargne ING' on 2026-09-06 and again on 2026-09-13, the later one flagged with no seasonal confound.

recommendations.title: Plan an extra refresh before the spring and summer attention peaks
recommendations.finding: Competitor current-account search terms show repeated isolated spikes through 2026, while ING's current-account signals cluster at the end of August and the start of September. Hypothesis to verify: ING's opening message may be arriving after rather than alongside these attention peaks.
recommendations.recommendation: Plan a second, lighter refresh of the current-account page opening message in spring or early summer, in addition to the September update, so the page is not refreshed only once a year.
recommendations.market_context: Belgium, 2021-09-12 to 2026-09-13: isolated spikes for 'KBC zichtrekening' on 2026-03-22 (value 27), 2026-05-17 (19) and 2026-07-26 (25).

recommendations.title: Keep sustainability wording specific and away from urgency copy
recommendations.finding: Sustainability and ESG is ING's largest named news theme of the last 90 days, and the notable headlines under it cover a climate case allowed to proceed and lending to oil companies. Themes are topics, not sentiment; the hypothesis to verify is that vague environmental wording on a page sits awkwardly next to a topic the press is actively covering.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep any sustainability reference on ING's pages specific and verifiable, place it apart from promotional urgency language, and avoid reusing it as a generic trust badge next to the pack offer.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING, 90-day headline window: esg_sustainability accounts for 5 of 20 headlines, including 'Milieudefensie mag van de rechter klimaatzaak tegen ING doorzetten' and 'ING hielp drie oliebedrijven aan bijna een miljard dollar, ondanks klimaatbelofte'.

recommendations.title: Anchor abstract digital claims on concrete product facts
recommendations.finding: Innovation and digital accounts for 2 of ING's 20 headlines of the last 90 days, the same count as product launches, while 10 sit under other. Themes are topics, not sentiment. Hypothesis to verify: if the pages lean on abstract digital-leadership wording, the current news themes give that wording little company and concrete product facts would be better anchored.
recommendations.recommendation: Replace abstract digital-leadership phrasing on the campaign pages with the concrete facts the page can support - what the pack includes and how sign-up works - keeping at most one digital claim.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING, 90-day headline window: innovation_digital 2 of 20 headlines and product_launch 2 of 20, against 10 under other.
